chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Do not wear a garment that you tuck (tazurruhu) and do not drape yourself with it (taddari'uhu) when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, and do not wear trousers unless you do not have an izar (lower garment), and do not wear the two khuff (leather socks) unless you do not have two sandals (na'lan). If the man has nothing with him except a qaba' (tunic), let him wear it inside out and do not put his hands into the sleeves of the qaba'. He narrated that."

key_terms.إِزَارٌ: A rectangular cloth used as a lower garment, typically unsewn
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَدَّرِعُهُ: To drape oneself with a garment
key_terms.تَزُرُّهُ: To tuck or gather the garment, implying a sewn or fitted style
key_terms.قَبَاءٌ: A tunic or coat, typically with sleeves

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for men's clothing during Ihram if they cannot wear the standard unsewn garments?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the practical jurisprudence of Ihram attire, emphasizing the prohibition of sewn garments (mukhaff) while allowing exceptions for necessity. It specifically addresses the scenario where a pilgrim possesses only a tunic (qaba'), instructing them to wear it inside-out without inserting their arms into the sleeves, thereby maintaining the spirit of simplicity and distinction from everyday dress. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity with practical adaptability in the absence of ideal conditions.
